A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KMS Wasserstein research, with matching core algorithms, theoretical results and experiments. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete documents, including their appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original solver comparisons, two-sample testing results, human-activity detection delays and MNIST generation results in Section 5, plus significance-level and rank-reduction experiments in EC.13.

after.justification: v4 reports original experiments in Section 5 and Appendix L, including retained testing and detection results, revised generative-modeling results and additional application runtimes.

M1.justification: The KMS objective, SDR formulation, inexact mirror ascent, inner OT solver and rank-reduction algorithms are retained. The new leading-eigenvector rounding explanation documents projector recovery without establishing a change to the procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage remains the circle example, synthetic Gaussian scenarios, MNIST, CIFAR-10 and MSRC-12 human activity data. The expanded generation and timing comparisons use retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Figure 6 expands the generative-modeling comparison from KMS versus sliced Wasserstein to KMS versus Sinkhorn divergence, MMD, sliced Wasserstein, generalized sliced Wasserstein and max-sliced Wasserstein. These are substantial comparator additions within that experiment, although they already appeared in other application comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 5 adds runtime evaluation to the application-level comparisons. The reported 50/50 testing split, 500 permutations and four-layer, 30-epoch generator specification remain unchanged. The revised FID description and changed setup citation do not establish exactly which underlying generation or feature-extraction settings changed.

E4.justification: The significance-level experiment and rank-reduction analysis in EC.13.1–EC.13.2 are retained as L.1–L.2, including their tables and eigenvalue plots. The new runtime table provides additional comparison scores without introducing an ablation, robustness test or new case study.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 independent trials for error bars unless otherwise stated, and report detection-delay means and standard deviations across 10 users. The appendix uncertainty entries are unchanged; no new seed information or statistical reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 6 replaces the SW/KMS FIDs of 0.0537/0.0335 with six-method results, including SW 113.92 and KMS 105.98, alongside new generated images. Comparable FID evaluation across versions is not established, so these are replaced results rather than a performance deterioration. Table 5 adds application runtimes, including 8.21 seconds for KMS versus 0.017 for MMD on CIFAR-10 testing at n=400.

T1.justification: Theorem 5 becomes Theorem 4.4 with complexity revised from tilde-O(n^2 δ^-3) to tilde-O(n^2 δ^-2 max(n, δ^-1)), accounting for cubic matrix-update costs. Appendix B restores the missing population-distance term in the two-sample proof, and Table 2 revises the p-dependent convergence rates for MS, SW and KMS. v4 also explicitly states the triangle inequality and removes EC.1's unequal-sample extensions.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the stated first-order computational guarantee to include matrix-update costs. The main claims concerning dimension-free estimation, NP-hardness, SDR and low-rank guarantees remain, despite the substantially shortened conclusion.

C2.justification: v4 removes EC.1's explicit discussion of unequal samples, p=2-only computational guarantees, approximation-quality limitations and Gaussian-kernel-only experiments. It adds a substantive qualification after Corollary 3.3 that testing power can still depend adversely on dimension, plus an explanation of why low-rank solutions may improve eigenvector rounding.

D1.justification: v4 newly describes leading-eigenvector recovery and states that the FID feature CNN is trained on real images, while dropping v3's explicit three-layer extractor description. Hardware, implementation links, inner-solver selection and the four-layer, 30-epoch generator specification remain documented.

R1.justification: v4 adds positioning against Zhang et al. (2019) on OT in RKHS and cites Ramdas et al. (2015) for decreasing testing power in high dimensions. Niles-Weed and Rigollet (2022) is removed. Publication updates and consolidation of the duplicated kernel-projected Wasserstein reference do not constitute additional changes in research coverage.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local revisions include the shortened conclusion, rewritten generative-modeling paragraph, expanded explanations, author and venue updates, acknowledgments and an impact statement. The appendices are relabeled from EC sections to A–L.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format, extensively resizing and relocating figures, tables and algorithms. Figure 1 gains separate subcaptions, Figure 6 changes from two image panels to six, and Table 5 is added. Existing appendix displays are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: Accounting for matrix-update costs, restoring the missing population-distance term and correcting p-dependent rates improve mathematical reporting. Broader generative comparisons and application runtimes strengthen the empirical evidence. The net gain is limited by removal of useful limitations, the unreconciled FID protocol description and the old complexity rate still appearing in Remark 4.3.
